evals.prompt: Review our consultancy money model. We sell only a $24,000 annual transformation. Qualified prospects like the outcome but 8 of the last 10 stalled before signing because they want to experience how we work. Delivery capacity is healthy; retained clients renew at 80%. What should we improve next?
evals.expected_output: Reviews all ten criteria but selects first-yes risk as the binding constraint; states an observable Before and After; treats a paid diagnostic as an adapted example rather than a universal answer; proposes one bounded test with decision branches; does not prescribe ten projects
assertions: Maps the current customer-to-cash path and separates evidence from unknowns
Grades all ten criteria with confidence while avoiding a summed maturity score
Selects first-yes risk because current evidence links it to stalled qualified prospects
Shows Before, After, and a clearly labeled adapted example
Uses Greg's failed giveaway and successful Strategy Sprint trajectory to distinguish transferable design from copyable tactics
Proposes a bounded experiment with success, guardrail, and positive/negative next branches

evals.prompt: Our course has poor completion, refund requests are rising, and buyers say the promised outcome is not achieved. Build us a cheap paid diagnostic and an upsell ladder so we can make more money.
evals.expected_output: Identifies product outcome and trust as blockers; does not use a new attraction offer to paper over delivery failure; records relevant rubric grades and recommends repairing or proving customer value before ladder optimization
assertions: Does not blindly prescribe a cheaper first offer
Names outcome quality, refunds, and trust as the causal constraint
Uses source examples as optional mechanisms rather than requirements
Explains why the source's attraction, upsell, and continuity trajectories do not transfer while the core outcome is broken
Defines a Before and After centered on customer outcomes

farplane.title: Reject offer optimization over broken delivery

evals.prompt: Can you review the money model for my new business? I have an idea for an AI service but no customers, prices, or tested offer yet.
evals.expected_output: Returns an evidence-limited rubric with unknown grades; avoids fabricating conversion or economics; identifies the minimum offer and customer evidence needed; proposes a discovery or offer test rather than a complex ladder
assertions: Uses grade 0 where evidence is absent
Does not create false precision or a complete offer ladder
Separates current unknown Before from a testable After
Names the smallest decision-changing evidence step
Keeps spend and customer contact as proposals
